Lewter</font></div><div style="text-align:right;text-indent:324pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">November&#160;5, 2026</font></div><div style="text-align:right;text-indent:324pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">Telephone&#58; (919) 968-2200</font></div><div style="text-align:right"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">        </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">Nasdaq Symbol&#58; ITIC</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:174%">FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE&#58;</font></div><div style="text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Chapel Hill, NC &#8211; Investors Title Company (Nasdaq&#58; ITIC) today announced results for the third quarter ended September&#160;30, 2026.  The Company reported net income of $9.4 million, or $4.97 per diluted share, compared to $12.2 million, or $6.45 per diluted share, for the prior-year period. </font></div><div style="text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Revenues increased 12.1% to $81.9 million, compared with $73.0 million in the prior-year period, driven primarily by growth in title insurance premiums and related fees.  Net premiums written and escrow and other title-related fees increased $13.0 million, or 21.2%, reflecting higher real estate transaction volumes and contributions from ongoing expansion initiatives.  </font></div><div style="text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Revenue growth was partially offset by net investment losses of $1.7 million, compared with net investment gains of $2.1 million in the prior-year period.  Current-year net investment losses primarily reflect impairment charges on certain fixed maturity securities amid higher interest rates, as well as lower realized gains on equity investments compared with the prior-year period.  Non-title services revenue declined $1.3 million, primarily due to lower like-kind exchange activity.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Operating expenses increased 21.7% to $70.5 million, compared with $57.9 million in the prior-year period, primarily reflecting higher agent commissions, claims provisions, and personnel expenses. Agent commissions increased commensurate with the growth in agency premiums.  The provision for claims rose primarily due to higher claims experience. Personnel expenses increased primarily as a result of geographic expansion and merit increases. Other operating expense categories remained relatively consistent with the prior-year period.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Income before income taxes decreased to $11.4 million, compared with $15.1 million in the prior-year quarter, primarily reflecting an unfavorable year-over-year change in net investment gains and losses.  Excluding the investment-related impacts, adjusted income before income taxes (non-GAAP) remained relatively unchanged at $13.1 million, compared with $13.0 million in the prior-year period (see Appendix A for a reconciliation to the most directly comparable GAAP measure).</font></div><div style="height:42.75pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:42.75pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div><div style="text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">For the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2026, net income increased 8.9% to $30.1 million, or $15.91 per diluted share, compared with $27.7 million, or $14.59 per diluted share, in the prior-year period.  Revenues increased 14.4% to $232.4 million, compared with $203.2 million in the prior-year period, reflecting continued growth in title insurance premiums and related fees.  Operating expenses increased 15.2% to $193.8 million, compared with $168.3 million in the prior-year period.   </font></div><div style="text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Income before income taxes increased 10.4% to $38.6 million, compared with $34.9 million in the prior-year period.  Excluding net investment gains, adjusted income before income taxes (non-GAAP) increased 9.2%</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%"> </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">to $34.9 million, compared with $32.0 million in the prior-year period (see Appendix A for a reconciliation to the most directly comparable GAAP measure).  </font></div><div style="text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Year-to-date results reflected many of the same factors affecting third-quarter performance, including higher title-related revenues, increased claims provisions, and higher operating expenses.  Comparisons were also affected by the absence of certain gains recognized in other revenue during the prior year and changes in net investment gains and losses.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Chairman J. Allen Fine commented, </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">We are pleased with the growth in title insurance revenues and continued ongoing initiatives. While higher claims experience and investment-related volatility decreased quarterly earnings, our underlying business continued to perform well, contributing to solid year-to-date results.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8221;</font></div><div style="text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Investors Title Company&#8217;s subsidiaries issue and underwrite title insurance policies.  The Company also provides investment management services and services in connection with tax-deferred exchanges of like-kind property.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="height:42.75pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:42.75pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div><div style="text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:150%;text-decoration:underline">Cautionary Statements Regarding Forward-Looking Statements</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:150%">Certain statements contained herein constitute forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995.  These statements may be identified by the use of words such as &#8220;plan,&#8221; &#8220;expect,&#8221; &#8220;aim,&#8221; &#8220;believe,&#8221; &#8220;project,&#8221; &#8220;anticipate,&#8221; &#8220;intend,&#8221; &#8220;estimate,&#8221; &#8220;should,&#8221; &#8220;could,&#8221; &#8220;would,&#8221; and other expressions that indicate future events and trends.  Such statements include, among others, any statements regarding the Company&#8217;s expected performance for future periods and the full year, the impact of order volumes on results in future quarters, future home price fluctuations, changes in home purchase or refinance demand, activity and the mix thereof, interest rate changes, expansion of the Company&#8217;s market presence, enhancement of competitive strengths, execution on expense management strategies, developments in housing affordability, wages, unemployment or overall economic conditions or statements regarding our actuarial assumptions and the application of recent historical claims experience to future periods.  These statements involve a number of risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from anticipated and historical results.  Such risks and uncertainties include, without limitation&#58;  the cyclical demand for title insurance due to changes in the residential and commercial real estate markets&#59; the occurrence of fraud, defalcation or misconduct&#59; variances between actual claims experience and underwriting and reserving assumptions, including the limited predictive power of historical claims experience&#59; declines in the performance of the Company&#8217;s investments&#59; changes in government regulations and policy, including as a result of the Trump administration such as policies related to tariffs and taxes and their impact on the macroeconomic environment&#59; changes in the economy&#59; the impact of inflation and responses by government regulators, including the Federal Reserve, such as business&#59; difficulties managing growth, whether organic or through acquisitions, and other considerations set forth under the caption &#8220;Risk Factors&#8221; in the Company&#8217;s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 as filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, and in subsequent filings.          </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times style="text-align:center"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Management uses various financial and operational measurements, including financial information not prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (&#34;GAAP&#34;), to analyze Company performance.  This includes adjusting revenues to remove the impact of net investment gains and losses, which are recognized in net income under GAAP.  Net investment gains and losses include realized gains and losses on sales of investment securities and changes in the estimated fair value of equity security investments.  Management believes that these measures are useful to evaluate the Company's internal operational performance from period to period because they eliminate the effects of external market fluctuations.  The Company also believes users of the financial results would benefit from having access to such information, and that certain of the Company&#8217;s peers make available similar information.  This information should not be used as a substitute for, or considered superior to, measures of financial performance prepared in accordance with GAAP, and may be different from similarly titled non-GAAP financial measures used by other companies.   </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New
